title: GAO 2001 NASA lessons-learned audit: a repository can exist without routine transfer into practice
summary: GAO’s 2001 survey of NASA’s lessons learned process is encoded as a correction-infrastructure audit: NASA had an agency-wide LLIS goal of avoiding relearning past lessons, but GAO reported fundamental weaknesses in collection, sharing, awareness, retrieval, and application. Temporal caution is explicit: the audit is historical, not a current performance claim.

status_history.note: Added as audit counterpart to NASA LLIS infrastructure record.

place.scope: NASA lessons learned process / GAO survey population

claims.claim: GAO reported that NASA procedures required managers to review, apply, document, and submit significant lessons learned, and that NASA’s principal agency-wide mechanism was LLIS, whose goal was to prevent NASA from relearning past lessons.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction or narrows its scope.

claims.claim: In the same 2001 survey, GAO found fundamental weaknesses in collection and sharing of lessons learned, including that lessons were not routinely identified, collected, or shared, and that LLIS was not a primary mechanism for many program/project managers.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction or narrows its scope.

claims.claim: GAO’s survey results recorded low reported LLIS use in the surveyed period, including 17.5 percent of respondents applying a lesson identified through LLIS and 23 percent submitting a lesson to LLIS in the past two years; these figures are historical audit data, not current LLIS performance metrics.
what_would_change_status: A reanalysis of the GAO survey or a newer audit changes the historical figures or provides updated current-performance data.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass government HTML extraction; no PDF/local archive hash yet
limitations: Temporal caution: 2001 audit must not be used to characterize current LLIS performance.
Survey response/interpretation details require second-pass review before quantitative synthesis.

type_payload.denominator_surface: population of NASA program/project managers surveyed by GAO
limits: not an audit of the content quality of individual LLIS records
type_payload.method_value: Keeps source-infrastructure records from becoming naive: memory surfaces must be audited for transfer, retrieval, application, and follow-through.
bias_or_lag_mechanisms_encoded: need to engineer lessons into processes

handling_notes: Frame as process audit, not blame against individual program managers.
Do not use historical frustration with lessons learned to dismiss the value of LLIS; use it to specify what future audits must test.

unknowns: No extraction of survey instrument/methodology details beyond one-pass web source.
No follow-up GAO/NASA response record yet.
next_actions: Find later NASA/GAO/OIG assessments, if any.
Pair with a sample LLIS lesson to trace recommendation infusion.
Add comparable audit records from other lessons-learned systems.
